chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, raised it to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

It was said to him, 'Some people claim that Al-Noura is disliked on the day of Friday.' So he said, 'It is not where you are going. Which cleanser is more purifying than Al-Noura on the day of Friday?'

key_terms.النُّورَةَ: Al-Noura (a lime paste used for hair removal)

ai.seo_question: Is it disliked to use Al-Noura for hair removal on Friday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) counters the view of some scholars who considered using *Al-Noura* (a lime-based paste for hair removal) disliked on Fridays. He elevates its status by declaring it the most purifying of all ablutions (*ath-hur*), thereby transforming it from a mere cosmetic act into a significant ritual of physical and spiritual cleanliness (*taharah*) befitting the blessed day. This reflects the Shia emphasis on maintaining personal hygiene as an integral part of worship and preparation for communal prayers.
